title: Enforcement Architecture
subtitle: Sidecar, gateway, middleware — latency and failure budgets
content:
🔌 Three Patterns (All Reviewed, All Fail-Closed)

  • Sidecar (rest-rego): reverse-proxy beside each service; JWT/OIDC or Azure Graph; <5ms overhead, 5000+ req/s; hot reload <1s; Prometheus + structured logs. Zero app code changes.
  • Gateway (Envoy + OPA): jwt_authn validates → x-jwt-payload to OPA via ext_authz gRPC → router forwards only on allow. failure_mode_allow: false, 200ms timeout.
  • Middleware (Keycloak + OPA): route table maps paths to resource:action; single Starlette/FastAPI middleware resolves user, checks OPA (local or sidecar), caches 5s, denies closed on OPA_FAIL_OPEN=false.

⏱️ Latency and Availability Budgets

  • Measure first: sidecar p99 vs gateway hop vs in-process Cedar. Cache decisions (5s TTL, fully-keyed) where freshness allows.
  • Timeouts are decisions: every PDP call has a deadline; deadline-exceeded = deny + alert, never queue-forever or allow.
  • Blast radius: gateway failure affects all routes (centralize carefully); sidecar failure affects one service; middleware local-mode survives network partitions.

🪜 Choosing (Decision Tree)

Zero code-change mandate? sidecar/gateway. Per-route permission vocabulary? middleware route table. Sub-5ms p99? in-process/embedded or fully-keyed cache. Multi-team gateway already? ext_authz filter reuses it. All three can front the same OPA/Cedar policies — pattern and policy are independent choices.

🎮 Try it in the Policy Lab → Compare the three patterns on flow, latency, and single-point-of-failure. Use the controls under the canvas to switch scenarios and watch the verdict change.

questions.question: Which reviewed setup adds <5ms overhead with zero app code changes?

options.text: rest-rego sidecar reverse-proxy with hot-reloaded Rego

questions.explanation: The sidecar's measured profile: <5ms, 5000+ req/s, hot reload <1s — the zero-code-change deployment story.

questions.question: In Envoy+OPA, what happens when OPA exceeds the 200ms timeout?
questions.explanation: Reviewed config is explicit: timeouts deny. Availability pressure never converts to unauthorized access.

questions.question: What does the middleware route table buy you?

options.text: One mapping of routes to resource:action strings, so handlers stay authZ-free and policy stays route-free

questions.explanation: The Keycloak-middleware RULES table is the PEP vocabulary: first-match-wins, empty permission = skip (public).

questions.question: Gateway PDP fails. Blast radius vs sidecar PDP fails?

options.text: Gateway: all routes denied (central); sidecar: one service denied (isolated)

questions.explanation: Centralization concentrates both consistency and failure. Both deny (fail-closed); the radius differs — design runbooks accordingly.

questions.question: Sub-5ms p99 authZ budget with fresh group data. Best lever?

options.text: In-process/embedded evaluation or fully-keyed short-TTL decision cache — measured, not guessed
Cache one global ALLOW for all users

questions.explanation: Latency budgets are met with locality (embedded PDP) or keyed caching — never by skipping decisions or sharing verdicts across subjects.

questions.question: The route table has overlapping regexes and first match wins. Hazard?

options.text: A broad early rule shadows stricter later ones — order specific-first and test overlaps

questions.explanation: First-match routing is priority routing. Untested overlaps silently downgrade strict routes to lax ones.

questions.question: A gateway PDP upgrade goes bad mid-deploy. Containment?

options.text: Canary plus instant rollback via bundle and config pin; per-route cutover bounds the radius
Upgrade everything at once for consistency
Hope the bad version is compatible

questions.explanation: Centralized enforcement centralizes failure. Upgrade like it can fail — because it can.

questions.question: Sidecar and app parse the JWT differently and disagree on identity. Result?

options.text: Authorization decisions on the wrong subject — one shared identity-extraction point

questions.explanation: Two identity truths means decisions about someone else. AuthN parsing happens once, upstream of all enforcement.
